selections.comment: A well contested finale in which two well-bred newcomers catch the eye. Given that both her half-brother and half-sister won their bumpers, the Charles Byrnes-trained RUN FOR MAHLER is of particular interest on her racecourse debut. Any market support, or indeed lack of, for the newcomer should be noted. The Willie Mullins-trained debutant Moon Mariner is also related to a previous bumper winner. While that latter horse proved a strong stayer, this stiff track shouldn't be too sharp for his half-sister here. Both Galileo Springs and Master Sydney have shown enough in their performances to date to suggest that they should once again play leading roles for their respective stables.

selections.comment: HALF SOVEREIGN hails from a pretty powerful yard in Karl Burke's, and she will certainly come on for the run after her debut 4th at Redcar last month. She was slowly getting into stride that day and did run a bit green throughout; therefore, she would have most likely learnt plenty from that experience and put that to good use here. She is probably the only one in the field who could go onto bigger and better things, and she should be landing this on the way beforehand. The Caddy Master has the two runs under his belt, which include a nice 3rd place finish at Redcar back in May. He can build on those two runs here and place behind a nicely bred sort who comes from a powerful yard. Folk Pageant will certainly need further time; however, she has a nice pedigree behind her, and she could fill the places here.

selections.comment: Not the strongest race on paper, but CAPTAIN HANLEY was unlucky not to finish better than 4th last time out when not getting a clear run with 2 furlongs to go. He was held at the rear throughout before making some smooth headway in the closing stages of the race, only to then get denied a clear run at a crucial part of the race. He still ran on well to claim the fourth spot and was an eye-catcher in the process. They have missed a prior engagement in Ireland for this race; therefore, he must have a really good chance here. Hill O Rue was a nice winner at Carlisle last time out, but this might be a stronger contest here; therefore, he will have to settle for a place finish here. And Penelope's Sister hails from the top yard around these parts; therefore, she can run well and fill the places here.

selections.comment: ABDUCTION was a nice winner at Hamilton last time out, and although the winning margin may not suggest this, he was probably an easier winner than it looks. He made some decent headway with a furlong to go before getting to the lead and keeping on in game fashion to get his head back in front for the first time since October 2023, when he was 11 lbs higher in the weights. He has a 4 lb raise in the weights here from last time, and on old form he can easily back up last time's win with another one here. Aberama Gold is obviously not the force of old when he was once rated 100+, but he has been creeping down the weights nicely recently and could easily strike off this current mark. He was once a winner of 96, and although that was almost two years ago, he could still have some of that talent in his locker and run well to come 2nd here. Orbital Chime has been running well since changing yards to Katie Scott's, and he could fill the places here.

A winner at Thirsk back in June when a well-fancied favourite that day, he then went on to back up the 11 lb raise in the weights with a game effort to win at Chester last time out. He only just got home that day but was always keeping on well towards the line. He has just the 2 lb raise to deal with here, and given his current form, he might be hard to peg back here. Wobwobwob was a winner off the mark of 87 previously; he has dropped down to a pretty attractive mark here, but he might have to settle for a 2nd place finish behind what looks to be a very progressive rival. Tarlac can fill the places for a yard, who are going pretty well at present.

And he did just that with a win off the mark of 67 at Hamilton last month, before backing that up again with a 2nd at Ayr a few weeks later. He was well beaten that day, but the winner was given a freebie on the front end; therefore, this bigger field should suit his running style a little more, as there will be more horses to take him into the race. Baby Rover got off the mark for the first time last time, and although he was the bottom weight here, he can build on that victory last time and place here. Unico has to carry top weight here but was a decent 2nd last time out; therefore, he can fill the places here.

Ebony Maw is another one running well, and having placed on two occasions since wind surgery back in March, she might have to unfortunately settle for another 3rd place finish here.

Times A Wastin has been progressive in bumpers of late and will find this much easier than his hurdle debut so could progress to complete the places.

She hated the soft ground when last seen but is on a good mark on her previous autumn form if her fitness holds up back from a break.

selections.comment: SMACKWATER JACK gained a first win in over 6 years last time and is taken to follow up as he remains unexposed over 3m for this stable. Though he's been raised 5lb to a mark of 97 he was capable of placing off 30lb higher at his best in the UK so is clearly still on a workable mark. Technology is another who has slipped to an attractive mark based on his old UK form and should threaten if his stamina holds up while Arrycan is also weighted to go close. He was disappointing over fences last time but is thrown in on his wins in that discipline and he proved himself capable in this sphere on his penultimate start.
